name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

content.content:
1	# JusPrin product definition
2	
3	**Status:** Canonical product direction for the `jusprin-dev` production branch.
4	
5	**Source:** Consolidated from product discovery on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Historical inspection evidence remains on that branch; see [POC reference](poc-reference.md).
6	
7	## Executive summary
8	
9	An AI agent can remove much of a slicer’s technical complexity, but it cannot eliminate the need for user interaction.
10	
11	The boundary is:
12	
13	> The user tells the system what is physically true, what the object means, and what outcome is wanted. The agent chooses the technical printing strategy. The user verifies consequential decisions and remains in control of the physical machine.
14	
15	This produces three classes of OrcaSlicer features:
16	
17	1. **User-decision surfaces must remain prominent.**
18	   These capture information the agent cannot reliably obtain: physical setup, functional intent, geometry meaning, aesthetic preferences, legal restrictions, and control over real-world actions.
19	
20	2. **Shared agent-and-user surfaces should be redesigned.**
21	   The agent proposes a solution, explains it, and draws attention to uncertainty. The user reviews the result visually instead of manipulating dozens of parameters.
22	
23	3. **Implementation settings can disappear from the primary interface.**
24	   The agent can usually manage line widths, speeds, infill mechanics, cooling, retraction, support parameters, and similar technical details.
25	
26	The final product should therefore retain nine primary surfaces:
27	
28	1. Project knowledge
29	2. Physical setup
30	3. Print intent
31	4. Objects and plates
32	5. Essential geometry editing
33	6. Local meaning and overrides
34	7. Print-plan verification
35	8. Sending a print and live control
36	9. Calibration and troubleshooting
37	
38	These are not remnants of a legacy slicer. They are the information and control boundary between a person, an AI agent, and a physical manufacturing process.
39	
40	The interface should not give every retained feature equal weight. Features fall into four visibility levels:
41	
42	1. **Default** — continuously visible in an ordinary project.
43	2. **Contextual** — appears when the project, current selection, or agent uncertainty makes it relevant.
44	3. **On demand** — available through Project details, More, or the expert layer.
45	4. **Interruptive** — normally hidden, but made prominent when a consequential warning, mismatch, or unresolved decision occurs.
46	
47	Frequency alone does not determine visibility. A control can be rarely used but interruptive because overlooking it would be costly or unsafe.
48	
49	---
50	
51	# 1. Why an AI agent sometimes lacks enough information
52	
53	Before deciding which UI to retain, it helps to distinguish the different reasons an agent cannot safely make a decision.
54	
55	## 1.1 The agent cannot observe physical reality reliably
56	
57	A slicer may say that a particular nozzle, plate, or filament is selected, but that does not prove it is installed.
58	
59	Examples include:
60	
61	- The build plate was changed manually.
62	- The AMS contains a different spool than expected.
63	- Filament is wet, old, tangled, or nearly empty.
64	- A hardened nozzle was replaced with a standard nozzle.
65	- Glue was or was not applied.
66	- The print bed is occupied.
67	- A previous print remains attached to the plate.
68	
69	The agent can detect some of these conditions using printer sensors or a camera, but uncertainty must remain visible.
70	
71	## 1.2 The agent does not know what the geometry means
72	
73	A mesh contains shapes, not intentions.
74	
75	The agent may identify a hole, thin wall, flat face, or overhang, but it does not inherently know whether that feature is:
76	
77	- A precision bearing surface
78	- A screw hole
79	- A snap fit
80	- A decorative opening
81	- A sacrificial support
82	- A face that must remain smooth
83	- A surface hidden after assembly
84	- A region intended to flex
85	- A deliberately thin membrane
86	
87	This is why essential geometry editing and semantic annotation must remain.
88	
89	## 1.3 The agent does not know the user’s priorities
90	
91	There is rarely one objectively correct slicing strategy. A user may prioritize:
92	
93	- Appearance
94	- Strength
95	- Dimensional accuracy
96	- Speed
97	- Material savings
98	- Heat resistance
99	- Flexibility
100	- Watertightness
101	- Minimal support marks
102	- A particular color arrangement
103	
104	These priorities can conflict. The agent needs the user to define what “good” means.
105	
106	## 1.4 Some decisions are subjective
107	
108	Seam placement, surface texture, layer visibility, support scars, color boundaries, and acceptable print time are personal judgments.
109	
110	An agent can recommend an option, but it cannot determine the user’s taste from the model alone.
111	
112	## 1.5 Some actions have consequential real-world effects
113	
114	Starting a print consumes material, occupies a machine, creates heat and motion, and may run unattended for hours. Firmware updates and calibration changes can alter the behavior of the printer.
115	
116	The agent can prepare these actions, but the user needs final authority over them.
117	
118	## 1.6 Some information concerns ownership, law, or safety
119	
120	The agent cannot invent or silently change:
121	
122	- Authorship
123	- Licensing
124	- Commercial-use permission
125	- Safety warnings
126	- Assembly instructions
127	- Bill-of-materials information
128	- Intended use
129	- Privacy and cloud-connectivity preferences
130	
131	These are authoritative project facts, not slicing parameters.
132	
133	---
134	
135	# 2. The surfaces that must remain
136	
137	## 2.0 Project-window hierarchy
138	
139	The Project window should not treat Prepare, Preview, and Info as three equal destinations.
140	
141	- **Prepare is the dominant, persistent workspace.** It is where users inspect the model, communicate intent, manipulate geometry, resolve uncertainty, and review the agent's plan.
142	- **Check print opens Orca Preview in a modal window.** Prepare remains underneath; closing Check returns focus to Prepare. It is a secondary action when the active plate has a valid slice.
143	- **Info becomes Project details.** It is a drawer opened from the project name or menu. The agent reads its contents continuously even when the drawer is closed.
144	- **Print opens OrcaSlicer's send dialog.** It never sends directly. The person's Send in that dialog remains the consequential commitment.
145	
146	The normal flow is:
147	
148	`Prepare -> Check print -> return to Prepare if correction is needed -> Print -> OrcaSlicer's send dialog -> the person presses Send`
149	
150	### Default Project-window composition
151	
152	The default window should contain:
153	
154	- Project name and saved/unsaved state
155	- Compact printer pointer: target printer, nozzle, build plate, and material
156	- Compact, editable intent summary
157	- Compact active plate/object summary
158	- 3D Prepare canvas
159	- Essential direct-manipulation tools
160	- Compact pinned agent plan
161	- Highest unresolved assumption, compromise, or risk
162	- Check print
163	- Print
164	- Consequential warnings when applicable
165	
166	The canvas is the primary human-agent collaboration surface. It must make the build plate and model visible, support camera rotation, pan, zoom, selection, and direct spatial manipulation, and show the changes the agent makes.
167	
168	The compact summaries should keep the governing assumptions visible without expanding full editors. Examples:
169	
170	> Decorative · appearance first · protect front surface · under 5 hours
171	
172	> Plate 1 · Fuzzy Heart · 1 copy · PLA Matte
173	
174	A one-object project should not permanently display a large object tree. A complete intent questionnaire should not remain expanded after it has been answered.
175	
176	In the Agent pane the intent summary and the pinned plan are the top of the setup card: the purpose in the person's words and the plan's headline in the agent's, each shown only once written, above the presets and estimates in force. The card warns only about a line it shows, as an annotation of that line, such as a plan the project has moved on from; other risks stay with the canvas, the chat and the printer chip (see the setup card in [Design System](design-system.md#components-and-states)).
177	
178	### Direct resolution of uncertainty
179	
180	Warnings should link to the user action that resolves them rather than expecting the user to translate them into legacy slicer controls:
181	
182	- `Support enters this hole` -> `Protect this opening`
183	- `Seam crosses a visible face` -> `Mark visible face`
184	- `Strength direction is unclear` -> `Show load direction`
185	- `Part may not fit` -> `Enter critical dimension`
186	- `Support may be hard to remove` -> `Adjust supports`
187	
188	Each feature still has one authoritative home, but summaries, warnings, and resolution actions may appear elsewhere. For example, Printer Configuration owns the installed hardware state while Prepare shows a compact pointer and any mismatch.
189	
190	## 2.1 Project knowledge
191	
192	This surface answers: **What is this project, and what does someone need to know about it?**
193	
194	OrcaSlicer exposes model descriptions, creator information, pictures, license information, profile notes, accessories, bills of materials, assembly guides, and other attachments.
195	
196	A project inspected during product discovery contained a safety instruction limiting it to electric tea lights. That information could affect how the agent evaluates material, temperature exposure, and intended use.
197	
198	### Why the agent cannot decide this alone
199	
200	The mesh does not contain reliable authorship, licensing, safety, assembly, or use-case information. An agent may extract clues, but it must not treat guesses as project facts.
201	
202	### What should remain
203	
204	- Project name and saved/unsaved state
205	- Project description
206	- Author and license
207	- Safety and usage instructions
208	- Reference pictures
209	- Assembly instructions
210	- Bill of materials and accessories
211	- Important profile notes
212	- Project save, version, backup, and ownership controls
213	
214	### What the agent should do
215	
216	The agent should read this material before planning the print, highlight contradictions, and ask about missing safety or assembly information when relevant.
217	
218	Only the project name and saved/unsaved state need to remain in the normal Project-window chrome. The rest belongs in the Project details drawer and surfaces automatically only when consequential:
219	
220	- Safety or usage warning: on import, when it affects planning, and before Print
221	- License restriction: when sharing, publishing, using commercially, or exporting
222	- Assembly instructions: for multi-part projects and plate organization
223	- Bill of materials or accessories: when non-printed components are required
224	- Reference image: when it clarifies orientation, color, or intended appearance
225	- Profile note: when the agent proposes deviating from it
226	- Recovery or version warning: when work is unsaved or versions conflict
227	
228	The user should not have to open Project details for its contents to influence the plan.
229	
230	---
231	
232	## 2.2 Physical printer setup
233	
234	This surface answers: **What hardware and material will actually perform the print?**
235	
236	### What should remain
237	
238	- Target printer
239	- Nozzle diameter and nozzle type
240	- Build-plate type
241	- Loaded filament and material
242	- Filament color
243	- AMS or multi-material slot mapping
244	- Printer availability and current condition
245	- Important mismatches between configuration and observed hardware
246	
247	### Why the agent cannot decide this alone
248	
249	Configured state and physical state can diverge. Selecting “PLA” in software does not establish that PLA is actually loaded, dry, correctly mapped, or compatible with the installed plate and nozzle.
250	
251	### What the agent should do
252	
253	- Discover printers and materials automatically
254	- Read AMS and printer state where available
255	- Compare observed state with the project
256	- Recommend compatible profiles
257	- Explain mismatches
258	- Ask the user only about unresolved physical facts
259	
260	The existing setup wizard’s enormous lists of printer and filament profiles should become hardware discovery followed by a short confirmation.
261	
262	---
263	
264	## 2.3 Print intent
265	
266	This surface answers: **What outcome does the user want?**
267	
268	Instead of beginning with hundreds of process parameters, the product should ask for meaningful requirements.
269	
270	### What should remain
271	
272	- Intended use
273	- Visual versus functional priority
274	- Strength direction
275	- Accuracy requirements
276	- Important dimensions or clearances
277	- Heat, chemical, outdoor, food-contact, or flexibility requirements
278	- Desired surface quality
279	- Maximum acceptable print time
280	- Material or color requirements
281	- Acceptable and unacceptable support contact
282	- Whether this is a prototype or final part
283	
284	### Why the agent cannot decide this alone
285	
286	The same model can legitimately be printed with different orientations, materials, wall structures, infill, supports, and tolerances depending on its purpose.
287	
288	A decorative prototype and a load-bearing final component may use identical geometry but require completely different plans.
289	
290	### What the agent should do
291	
292	Translate intent into technical settings. For example:
293	
294	> “This is a visible decorative object, so I oriented it to protect the front surface, moved the seam to the rear, and accepted a longer print to reduce visible layer artifacts.”
295	
296	The user should judge that reasoning without having to configure every underlying value.
297	
298	The full intent editor should appear during project creation, import, or when requirements are incomplete. Afterward, Prepare should retain only a compact editable summary. Specialized questions such as food contact, flexibility, critical clearances, and protected support surfaces should appear contextually rather than in every project.
299	
300	---

7. Print-plan verification
8. Sending a print and live control
9. Calibration and troubleshooting

These are not remnants of a legacy slicer. They are the information and control boundary between a person, an AI agent, and a physical manufacturing process.

The interface should not give every retained feature equal weight. Features fall into four visibility levels:

1. **Default** — continuously visible in an ordinary project.
2. **Contextual** — appears when the project, current selection, or agent uncertainty makes it relevant.
3. **On demand** — available through Project details, More, or the expert layer.
4. **Interruptive** — normally hidden, but made prominent when a consequential warning, mismatch, or unresolved decision occurs.

Frequency alone does not determine visibility. A control can be rarely used but interruptive because overlooking it would be costly or unsafe.

---

# 1. Why an AI agent sometimes lacks enough information

Before deciding which UI to retain, it helps to distinguish the different reasons an agent cannot safely make a decision.

## 1.1 The agent cannot observe physical reality reliably

A slicer may say that a particular nozzle, plate, or filament is selected, but that does not prove it is installed.

Examples include:

- The build plate was changed manually.
- The AMS contains a different spool than expected.
- Filament is wet, old, tangled, or nearly empty.
- A hardened nozzle was replaced with a standard nozzle.
- Glue was or was not applied.
- The print bed is occupied.
- A previous print remains attached to the plate.

The agent can detect some of these conditions using printer sensors or a camera, but uncertainty must remain visible.

## 1.2 The agent does not know what the geometry means

A mesh contains shapes, not intentions.

The agent may identify a hole, thin wall, flat face, or overhang, but it does not inherently know whether that feature is:

- A precision bearing surface
- A screw hole
- A snap fit
- A decorative opening
- A sacrificial support
- A face that must remain smooth
- A surface hidden after assembly
- A region intended to flex
- A deliberately thin membrane

This is why essential geometry editing and semantic annotation must remain.

## 1.3 The agent does not know the user’s priorities

There is rarely one objectively correct slicing strategy. A user may prioritize:

- Appearance
- Strength
- Dimensional accuracy
- Speed
- Material savings
- Heat resistance
- Flexibility
- Watertightness
- Minimal support marks
- A particular color arrangement

These priorities can conflict. The agent needs the user to define what “good” means.

## 1.4 Some decisions are subjective

Seam placement, surface texture, layer visibility, support scars, color boundaries, and acceptable print time are personal judgments.

An agent can recommend an option, but it cannot determine the user’s taste from the model alone.

## 1.5 Some actions have consequential real-world effects

Starting a print consumes material, occupies a machine, creates heat and motion, and may run unattended for hours. Firmware updates and calibration changes can alter the behavior of the printer.

The agent can prepare these actions, but the user needs final authority over them.

## 1.6 Some information concerns ownership, law, or safety

The agent cannot invent or silently change:

- Authorship
- Licensing
- Commercial-use permission
- Safety warnings
- Assembly instructions
- Bill-of-materials information
- Intended use
- Privacy and cloud-connectivity preferences

These are authoritative project facts, not slicing parameters.

---

# 2. The surfaces that must remain

## 2.0 Project-window hierarchy

The Project window should not treat Prepare, Preview, and Info as three equal destinations.

- **Prepare is the dominant, persistent workspace.** It is where users inspect the model, communicate intent, manipulate geometry, resolve uncertainty, and review the agent's plan.
- **Check print opens Orca Preview in a modal window.** Prepare remains underneath; closing Check returns focus to Prepare. It is a secondary action when the active plate has a valid slice.
- **Info becomes Project details.** It is a drawer opened from the project name or menu. The agent reads its contents continuously even when the drawer is closed.
- **Print opens OrcaSlicer's send dialog.** It never sends directly. The person's Send in that dialog remains the consequential commitment.

The normal flow is:

`Prepare -> Check print -> return to Prepare if correction is needed -> Print -> OrcaSlicer's send dialog -> the person presses Send`

### Default Project-window composition

The default window should contain:

- Project name and saved/unsaved state
- Compact printer pointer: target printer, nozzle, build plate, and material
- Compact, editable intent summary
- Compact active plate/object summary
- 3D Prepare canvas
- Essential direct-manipulation tools
- Compact pinned agent plan
- Highest unresolved assumption, compromise, or risk
- Check print
- Print
- Consequential warnings when applicable

The canvas is the primary human-agent collaboration surface. It must make the build plate and model visible, support camera rotation, pan, zoom, selection, and direct spatial manipulation, and show the changes the agent makes.

The compact summaries should keep the governing assumptions visible without expanding full editors. Examples:

> Decorative · appearance first · protect front surface · under 5 hours

> Plate 1 · Fuzzy Heart · 1 copy · PLA Matte

A one-object project should not permanently display a large object tree. A complete intent questionnaire should not remain expanded after it has been answered.

In the Agent pane the intent summary and the pinned plan are the top of the setup card: the purpose in the person's words and the plan's headline in the agent's, each shown only once written, above the presets and estimates in force. The card warns only about a line it shows, as an annotation of that line, such as a plan the project has moved on from; other risks stay with the canvas, the chat and the printer chip (see the setup card in [Design System](design-system.md#components-and-states)).

### Direct resolution of uncertainty

Warnings should link to the user action that resolves them rather than expecting the user to translate them into legacy slicer controls:

- `Support enters this hole` -> `Protect this opening`
- `Seam crosses a visible face` -> `Mark visible face`
- `Strength direction is unclear` -> `Show load direction`
- `Part may not fit` -> `Enter critical dimension`
- `Support may be hard to remove` -> `Adjust supports`

Each feature still has one authoritative home, but summaries, warnings, and resolution actions may appear elsewhere. For example, Printer Configuration owns the installed hardware state while Prepare shows a compact pointer and any mismatch.

## 2.1 Project knowledge

This surface answers: **What is this project, and what does someone need to know about it?**

OrcaSlicer exposes model descriptions, creator information, pictures, license information, profile notes, accessories, bills of materials, assembly guides, and other attachments.

A project inspected during product discovery contained a safety instruction limiting it to electric tea lights. That information could affect how the agent evaluates material, temperature exposure, and intended use.

### Why the agent cannot decide this alone

The mesh does not contain reliable authorship, licensing, safety, assembly, or use-case information. An agent may extract clues, but it must not treat guesses as project facts.

### What should remain

- Project name and saved/unsaved state
- Project description
- Author and license
- Safety and usage instructions
- Reference pictures
- Assembly instructions
- Bill of materials and accessories
- Important profile notes
- Project save, version, backup, and ownership controls

### What the agent should do

The agent should read this material before planning the print, highlight contradictions, and ask about missing safety or assembly information when relevant.

Only the project name and saved/unsaved state need to remain in the normal Project-window chrome. The rest belongs in the Project details drawer and surfaces automatically only when consequential:

- Safety or usage warning: on import, when it affects planning, and before Print
- License restriction: when sharing, publishing, using commercially, or exporting
- Assembly instructions: for multi-part projects and plate organization
- Bill of materials or accessories: when non-printed components are required
- Reference image: when it clarifies orientation, color, or intended appearance
- Profile note: when the agent proposes deviating from it
- Recovery or version warning: when work is unsaved or versions conflict

The user should not have to open Project details for its contents to influence the plan.

---

## 2.2 Physical printer setup

This surface answers: **What hardware and material will actually perform the print?**

### What should remain

- Target printer
- Nozzle diameter and nozzle type
- Build-plate type
- Loaded filament and material
- Filament color
- AMS or multi-material slot mapping
- Printer availability and current condition
- Important mismatches between configuration and observed hardware

### Why the agent cannot decide this alone

Configured state and physical state can diverge. Selecting “PLA” in software does not establish that PLA is actually loaded, dry, correctly mapped, or compatible with the installed plate and nozzle.

### What the agent should do

- Discover printers and materials automatically
- Read AMS and printer state where available
- Compare observed state with the project
- Recommend compatible profiles
- Explain mismatches
- Ask the user only about unresolved physical facts

The existing setup wizard’s enormous lists of printer and filament profiles should become hardware discovery followed by a short confirmation.

---

## 2.3 Print intent

This surface answers: **What outcome does the user want?**

Instead of beginning with hundreds of process parameters, the product should ask for meaningful requirements.

### What should remain

- Intended use
- Visual versus functional priority
- Strength direction
- Accuracy requirements
- Important dimensions or clearances
- Heat, chemical, outdoor, food-contact, or flexibility requirements
- Desired surface quality
- Maximum acceptable print time
- Material or color requirements
- Acceptable and unacceptable support contact
- Whether this is a prototype or final part

### Why the agent cannot decide this alone

The same model can legitimately be printed with different orientations, materials, wall structures, infill, supports, and tolerances depending on its purpose.

A decorative prototype and a load-bearing final component may use identical geometry but require completely different plans.

### What the agent should do

Translate intent into technical settings. For example:

> “This is a visible decorative object, so I oriented it to protect the front surface, moved the seam to the rear, and accepted a longer print to reduce visible layer artifacts.”

The user should judge that reasoning without having to configure every underlying value.

The full intent editor should appear during project creation, import, or when requirements are incomplete. Afterward, Prepare should retain only a compact editable summary. Specialized questions such as food contact, flexibility, critical clearances, and protected support surfaces should appear contextually rather than in every project.

---

1	=== f46e5ac05f JusPrin Cloud account: credits, the first launch, and sign-in by email and Google at jusprinv2.obico.io
2	Credits. The app shows and spends JusPrin Cloud credits; every credit is the
3	same, and a balance is one number of credits.
4	- Model pickers show each model's price, and are greyed once the chat has a
5	  message. The balance shows as a ring with a hover panel: one bar per lot,
6	  grouped by expiry, bought credits included. A message that can't be paid
7	  for offers "Get more credits"; a 402 from the gateway ends in a failed card.
8	  "About 25 credits left" shows once at 25 credits or less.
9	- A new account chat starts on Expert while a first-month lot is live, and on
10	  Standard after it. A Standard chat leaves out the picture tools; a picture
11	  there shows as a warning on its chip, with Remove.
12	- Turns the app starts itself send X-JusPrin-Request: note and run on Expert
13	  without changing the chat's model. RecordConversion turns one provider
14	  format's stored turn into the other's, byte for byte, so caches still hit.
15	- A turn that polls for its own slice is answered with busy, and the third
16	  refused poll ends the turn.
17	- Print history has a report form with a photo; every report earns 25 credits.
18	The gateway side (ledger, Chargebee, the pricing page) is on tsd-enterprise
19	branch claude/credits-ledger. The welcome-back window's kept-price box stays
20	hidden behind V1_PRICE_CARRIES_OVER until then.
21	
22	First launch: Welcome, then Printers, then Home, as on the canvas's "On
23	boarding experience" page.
24	- Welcome: the lockup, a placeholder clip with its photo credits, "The AI
25	  slicer that fixes failed prints." and four doors: sign in, your own API key,
26	  Claude Code or Claude Desktop, and Just slice.
27	- Printers: "Bring your printers from OrcaSlicer?" when an OrcaSlicer folder
28	  sits beside the data folder; otherwise the Agent page's add-printer form,
29	  with "Skip, use a default", which installs Generic Klipper and marks that
30	  printer "assumed" on its Home card. Skipped when a JusPrin v1 import or an
31	  opened file already brought a printer. After an import, a result screen
32	  lists each printer and process preset as imported, imported as
33	  "<name> (Orca copy)", or not imported with the reason. OrcaSlicer's
34	  PresetBundle::import_presets is unchanged: OrcaImport.cpp gives a taken name
35	  a renamed copy first, so it has nothing to ask.
36	- Home: an Agent group above Printers shows "Set up the agent" with the three
37	  doors, or the account and its credit bars after signing in.
38	- OnboardingModel decides the step from saved progress; onboarding is saved as
39	  completed only once Home is reached, and the earlier "dismissed" status
40	  counts as completed. ShellController::open_preferences can open Preferences
41	  for one task and report "key", "tool" or nothing.
42	- The add-printer form is AgentUI's AddPrinterForm in a shadow root, and its
43	  host is the printer chat's conversation with no thread and no model: it has
44	  no messages and no tool call to finish.
45	- resources/jusprin/welcome/welcome-clip.mp4 is a PLACEHOLDER animatic, to be
46	  replaced by a recording of the real app; its two #3DBenchy photos are
47	  CC BY 2.0, credited in that folder's README and on the welcome.
48	
49	Sign-in. The door on the welcome and on Home offers "Continue with Google" and
50	"Continue with email".
51	- Email signs in through django-allauth's API for apps under
52	  ent/jusprin/v2/auth/: "Email me a 6-digit code" (which also makes the
53	  account for a new address) or a password with Forgot password. It brings the
54	  same OAuth token as the browser sign-in. Wrong code, a spent code, too many
55	  codes, wrong password and too many tries stay on their step; anything else
56	  ends with one generic error.
57	- Google opens /accounts/google/login/ with next= the authorize address, so
58	  the browser goes straight to Google and back. PKCE, state and the loopback
59	  callback are unchanged.
60	- JusPrin is a syndicate of its own on the server, which picks it by host: the
61	  gateway and the sign-in server move from app.obico.io to jusprinv2.obico.io.
62	  v1's Obico account is no longer a JusPrin account, so the v1 import no
63	  longer carries v1's token or server, and v1 users sign up again.
64	- Until jusprinv2.obico.io is live in production, a build signs in only with
65	  JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT pointing at staging (jusprinv2-stg.obico.io).
66	
67	Also: save_onboarding passed a const char* to AppConfig::set, which saved
68	every field as "true". The shell harness fixes three older macOS defects (a
69	null title bar menu in --print-history, page reads cut at about 1000
70	characters, fake-printer control writes within one second ignored), and
71	--fresh-example signs in by email against a stand-in gateway. A dialog log
72	line in DialogListeners.cpp no longer names OrcaSlicer, which AgentUI's
73	wording guard flagged.
74	
75	Tested on macOS: agent_bridge_tests (554 cases, with the coordinator fix that
76	follows), jusprin_tests (222), workspace (51), brand (49), Home page Vitest
77	(154), Agent page Vitest (666), the shell harness default run (600 checks) and
78	--fresh-example (51 checks). Windows and Linux were not run.
79	
80	Squashed from claude/elated-sutherland-84a741 (19 commits, 48ec76705d to
81	4b16e4b1eb), merged onto the printer card change.

83	=== ac55c2961a Sign in to a JusPrin account, and bring a JusPrin v1 setup along
84	A JusPrin account is now an Agent provider beside the API keys. Its models
85	are aliases ("Slicer 1") that JusPrin's gateway serves in the Anthropic or
86	the OpenAI Responses format, as the account is assigned.
87	
88	- Provider: a "jusprin" row (ProviderProfile.hpp) whose credential is the
89	  account's OAuth token. Every request names its turn and kind
90	  (X-JusPrin-Turn, X-JusPrin-Request) so the gateway charges once per turn
91	  and never for a title; 401/403 read as a sign-in that ended, 402 as a
92	  used-up allowance.
93	- Format per chat: the model list says which format each alias is served
94	  in, and a chat is fixed to the format of its first request
95	  (ChatModelChoice.format in the project document), so a changed A/B
96	  assignment reaches new chats only.
97	- Sign-in (CloudAccount, CloudSignInMachine): authorization code with
98	  PKCE in the system browser, answered on a loopback port by OrcaSlicer's
99	  own OAuthJob and HttpServer, called rather than edited. A token is kept
100	  only after the server says who the account is and which models it gets.
101	  The setup service carries it, so Preferences shows the account row's
102	  states (signed out, waiting for the browser, signed in, sign-in ended),
103	  and Sign out revokes the token. The server is jusprin_server/base_url,
104	  the setting v1 used, so staging or a self-hosted server is one setting.
105	- v1 import (V1Import): on the first start with no settings of its own,
106	  JusPrin 2 copies v1's user presets, Bambu's network settings and v1's
107	  settings file, whose sign-in becomes the account's token. v1's folder is
108	  only read. The welcome-back window (canvas boards V1-01 to V1-03) shows
109	  what came along once, checks the imported sign-in, and waits until no
110	  OrcaSlicer start-up dialog is open.
111	
112	- Images for the model (ImageThumbnail.cpp, image_for_model): an attached
113	  image over a 2576-pixel long edge or 2 MiB is scaled down and re-encoded
114	  (JPEG, or PNG when transparent) before any provider is sent it. Claude
115	  looks at no more than 2576 pixels, and its API takes at most 10 MB of
116	  base64 per image, which a 10 MiB photo exceeds once encoded.
117	
118	OrcaSlicer-owned code: one call in GUI_App::init_app_config, before the
119	settings file is read. Against current upstream it merges cleanly next to
120	the line upstream changed there.
121	
122	Tests: agent_bridge_tests (447 cases, including test_cloud_account and
123	test_v1_import) and the AgentUI vitest suite (638) pass. Checked end to end
124	against a local gateway and against staging.

128	=== b0a2fe3b08 First launch and File › Import: a clearer sign-up offer, and OrcaSlicer's printers brought in now or later, each one chosen, with one profile reload
129	Sign-up and the welcome:
130	- The offer reads "Sign up and get 500 free credits", says they last the

132	  button reads "Sign up free" with "Already have an account? Sign in"

162	- A window over the current screen finds OrcaSlicer's folder the same
163	  way, lists its printers with tick boxes and marks the ones JusPrin
164	  already has as "Already in JusPrin". A preset counts as already there

169	- It leaves the open project's printer, filaments and process as they

=== f46e5ac05f JusPrin Cloud account: credits, the first launch, and sign-in by email and Google at jusprinv2.obico.io
Credits. The app shows and spends JusPrin Cloud credits; every credit is the
same, and a balance is one number of credits.
- Model pickers show each model's price, and are greyed once the chat has a
  message. The balance shows as a ring with a hover panel: one bar per lot,
  grouped by expiry, bought credits included. A message that can't be paid
  for offers "Get more credits"; a 402 from the gateway ends in a failed card.
  "About 25 credits left" shows once at 25 credits or less.
- A new account chat starts on Expert while a first-month lot is live, and on
  Standard after it. A Standard chat leaves out the picture tools; a picture
  there shows as a warning on its chip, with Remove.
- Turns the app starts itself send X-JusPrin-Request: note and run on Expert
  without changing the chat's model. RecordConversion turns one provider
  format's stored turn into the other's, byte for byte, so caches still hit.
- A turn that polls for its own slice is answered with busy, and the third
  refused poll ends the turn.
- Print history has a report form with a photo; every report earns 25 credits.
The gateway side (ledger, Chargebee, the pricing page) is on tsd-enterprise
branch claude/credits-ledger. The welcome-back window's kept-price box stays
hidden behind V1_PRICE_CARRIES_OVER until then.

First launch: Welcome, then Printers, then Home, as on the canvas's "On
boarding experience" page.
- Welcome: the lockup, a placeholder clip with its photo credits, "The AI
  slicer that fixes failed prints." and four doors: sign in, your own API key,
  Claude Code or Claude Desktop, and Just slice.
- Printers: "Bring your printers from OrcaSlicer?" when an OrcaSlicer folder
  sits beside the data folder; otherwise the Agent page's add-printer form,
  with "Skip, use a default", which installs Generic Klipper and marks that
  printer "assumed" on its Home card. Skipped when a JusPrin v1 import or an
  opened file already brought a printer. After an import, a result screen
  lists each printer and process preset as imported, imported as
  "<name> (Orca copy)", or not imported with the reason. OrcaSlicer's
  PresetBundle::import_presets is unchanged: OrcaImport.cpp gives a taken name
  a renamed copy first, so it has nothing to ask.
- Home: an Agent group above Printers shows "Set up the agent" with the three
  doors, or the account and its credit bars after signing in.
- OnboardingModel decides the step from saved progress; onboarding is saved as
  completed only once Home is reached, and the earlier "dismissed" status
  counts as completed. ShellController::open_preferences can open Preferences
  for one task and report "key", "tool" or nothing.
- The add-printer form is AgentUI's AddPrinterForm in a shadow root, and its
  host is the printer chat's conversation with no thread and no model: it has
  no messages and no tool call to finish.
- resources/jusprin/welcome/welcome-clip.mp4 is a PLACEHOLDER animatic, to be
  replaced by a recording of the real app; its two #3DBenchy photos are
  CC BY 2.0, credited in that folder's README and on the welcome.

Sign-in. The door on the welcome and on Home offers "Continue with Google" and
"Continue with email".
- Email signs in through django-allauth's API for apps under
  ent/jusprin/v2/auth/: "Email me a 6-digit code" (which also makes the
  account for a new address) or a password with Forgot password. It brings the
  same OAuth token as the browser sign-in. Wrong code, a spent code, too many
  codes, wrong password and too many tries stay on their step; anything else
  ends with one generic error.
- Google opens /accounts/google/login/ with next= the authorize address, so
  the browser goes straight to Google and back. PKCE, state and the loopback
  callback are unchanged.
- JusPrin is a syndicate of its own on the server, which picks it by host: the
  gateway and the sign-in server move from app.obico.io to jusprinv2.obico.io.
  v1's Obico account is no longer a JusPrin account, so the v1 import no
  longer carries v1's token or server, and v1 users sign up again.
- Until jusprinv2.obico.io is live in production, a build signs in only with
  JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT pointing at staging (jusprinv2-stg.obico.io).

Also: save_onboarding passed a const char* to AppConfig::set, which saved
every field as "true". The shell harness fixes three older macOS defects (a
null title bar menu in --print-history, page reads cut at about 1000
characters, fake-printer control writes within one second ignored), and
--fresh-example signs in by email against a stand-in gateway. A dialog log
line in DialogListeners.cpp no longer names OrcaSlicer, which AgentUI's
wording guard flagged.

Tested on macOS: agent_bridge_tests (554 cases, with the coordinator fix that
follows), jusprin_tests (222), workspace (51), brand (49), Home page Vitest
(154), Agent page Vitest (666), the shell harness default run (600 checks) and
--fresh-example (51 checks). Windows and Linux were not run.

Squashed from claude/elated-sutherland-84a741 (19 commits, 48ec76705d to
4b16e4b1eb), merged onto the printer card change.

=== ac55c2961a Sign in to a JusPrin account, and bring a JusPrin v1 setup along
A JusPrin account is now an Agent provider beside the API keys. Its models
are aliases ("Slicer 1") that JusPrin's gateway serves in the Anthropic or
the OpenAI Responses format, as the account is assigned.

- Provider: a "jusprin" row (ProviderProfile.hpp) whose credential is the
  account's OAuth token. Every request names its turn and kind
  (X-JusPrin-Turn, X-JusPrin-Request) so the gateway charges once per turn
  and never for a title; 401/403 read as a sign-in that ended, 402 as a
  used-up allowance.
- Format per chat: the model list says which format each alias is served
  in, and a chat is fixed to the format of its first request
  (ChatModelChoice.format in the project document), so a changed A/B
  assignment reaches new chats only.
- Sign-in (CloudAccount, CloudSignInMachine): authorization code with
  PKCE in the system browser, answered on a loopback port by OrcaSlicer's
  own OAuthJob and HttpServer, called rather than edited. A token is kept
  only after the server says who the account is and which models it gets.
  The setup service carries it, so Preferences shows the account row's
  states (signed out, waiting for the browser, signed in, sign-in ended),
  and Sign out revokes the token. The server is jusprin_server/base_url,
  the setting v1 used, so staging or a self-hosted server is one setting.
- v1 import (V1Import): on the first start with no settings of its own,
  JusPrin 2 copies v1's user presets, Bambu's network settings and v1's
  settings file, whose sign-in becomes the account's token. v1's folder is
  only read. The welcome-back window (canvas boards V1-01 to V1-03) shows
  what came along once, checks the imported sign-in, and waits until no
  OrcaSlicer start-up dialog is open.

- Images for the model (ImageThumbnail.cpp, image_for_model): an attached
  image over a 2576-pixel long edge or 2 MiB is scaled down and re-encoded
  (JPEG, or PNG when transparent) before any provider is sent it. Claude
  looks at no more than 2576 pixels, and its API takes at most 10 MB of
  base64 per image, which a 10 MiB photo exceeds once encoded.

OrcaSlicer-owned code: one call in GUI_App::init_app_config, before the
settings file is read. Against current upstream it merges cleanly next to
the line upstream changed there.

Tests: agent_bridge_tests (447 cases, including test_cloud_account and
test_v1_import) and the AgentUI vitest suite (638) pass. Checked end to end
against a local gateway and against staging.

- The printer list and result lines are one component,

- Both pages show "Importing..." with the other buttons disabled and send
  the request only after a second frame and 50 ms
  (WebShared/afterPaint.ts). Sent sooner, the import blocked the UI
  thread before it put the label on screen.

Home:
- A printer card with no connection ever set up hides the status row and
  says "Connect it to send prints straight from JusPrin" beside Connect.
- The signed-out "Set up the agent" card says what signing up gets.

AGENTS.md: removes "Landing a branch on jusprin-newui", the rule that
feature branches land with git merge --no-ff and never a squash.

AgentUI vitest (687, wording.test.ts included), HomeUI vitest (155), both
tsc runs clean. In the built app with copies of an OrcaSlicer folder:
signed out, the welcome, email code and password, the import screen with
printers unticked, "Choose my printer instead", the reading spinner, Skip,

name: JusPrin release

# Builds JusPrin from one commit and uploads the files to a DRAFT GitHub
# release. It never publishes anything.
#
# - The version is the one in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp, and
#   the draft is tagged jusprin/v<version>, as JusPrin 1.4.0 was (the repo
#   still holds OrcaSlicer's own v2.x tags). GitHub creates that tag only when
#   the draft is published, by hand, on the Releases page. JusPrin's update
#   check reads the public release list, which never includes drafts, so
#   users see nothing until then.
# - It stops if that version is already released, is not above every
#   released JusPrin version, or its tag already exists
#   (Packaging/release.mjs), and if
#   Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md, the notes the draft starts with and
#   that the app shows under "What's new", is missing.
# - Running it again for the same version replaces the draft's files.
# - Files: Windows x64 installer and portable zip, macOS universal disk image,
#   Linux x64 AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
# - Only the release publisher can run it: the repo variable
#   JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER, or kennethjiang when it is unset.
# - Signing: macOS when "sign_macos" is ticked, with the Apple secrets JusPrin
#   1.x used. Windows builds are unsigned. An unsigned draft says so in its
#   title.
#
# Start it from Actions > JusPrin release > Run workflow (the file must also
# be on the default branch for that button), or by pushing a branch named
# jusprin-release/<anything>.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign_macos:
        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
        type: boolean
        default: false
  push:
    branches:
      - 'jusprin-release/**'

permissions:
  contents: write   # create the draft and upload its files
  actions: read

concurrency:
  group: jusprin-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    name: Check the version
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.check.outputs.tag }}
      prerelease: ${{ steps.check.outputs.prerelease }}
      draft_id: ${{ steps.check.outputs.draft_id }}
    steps:
      - name: Only the release publisher
        env:
          PUBLISHER: ${{ vars.JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER || 'kennethjiang' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_ACTOR" != "$PUBLISHER" ]; then
            echo "::error::Only @$PUBLISHER may make a JusPrin release (this run is @$GITHUB_ACTOR's)."
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Test the release checks
        run: node --test src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.test.mjs

      - name: Check the version against the releases
        id: check

# JusPrin's publisher and version, for everything the build stamps with them:
# the Windows version resource (src/dev-utils/platform/msw/OrcaSlicer.rc.in)
# and the package (packaging.cmake). The top-level CMakeLists.txt includes
# this file right after version.inc, before any of them is configured.
#
# The product name is SLIC3R_APP_NAME, which version.inc already sets to
# JusPrin.

set(JUSPRIN_VENDOR "Obico")

# JusPrin's version lives in one place, Version.hpp; the release workflow
# reads it from there too.
set(_jusprin_version_header "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp")
file(STRINGS "${_jusprin_version_header}" _jusprin_version_line REGEX "kVersion\\[\\] = \"")
if (NOT _jusprin_version_line MATCHES "\"(([0-9]+)\\.([0-9]+)\\.([0-9]+)[^\"]*)\"")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "No kVersion = \"X.Y.Z\" line in ${_jusprin_version_header}")

content.content:
# JusPrin's package identity. The top-level CMakeLists.txt includes this file
# just before include(CPack), so each value set here replaces OrcaSlicer's.
#
# Without it the Windows installer calls itself OrcaSlicer by SoftFever,
# version 2.4.2, and uses OrcaSlicer's uninstall key. Because OrcaSlicer turns
# on CPACK_NSIS_ENABLE_UNINSTALL_BEFORE_INSTALL, that installer would first
# uninstall a real OrcaSlicer. With the key "JusPrin", the one JusPrin 1.x
# used, installing 2.x replaces 1.x instead.
#
# The macOS app and the Linux AppImage get the same identity in the release
# workflow (.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml), which renames and edits
# them after the build.
#
# The version and publisher come from identity.cmake, which the Windows
# version resource of orca-slicer.exe reads too.

set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION_MAJOR "${JUSPRIN_VERSION_MAJOR}")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION_MINOR "${JUSPRIN_VERSION_MINOR}")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION_PATCH "${JUSPRIN_VERSION_PATCH}")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION "${JUSPRIN_VERSION}")

set(CPACK_PACKAGE_NAME "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VENDOR "${JUSPRIN_VENDOR}")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_DESCRIPTION_SUMMARY "JusPrin, the AI-piloted 3D printing slicer built on OrcaSlicer")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_HOMEPAGE_URL "https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_INSTALL_DIRECTORY "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_INSTALL_REGISTRY_KEY "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_NSIS_DISPLAY_NAME "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_NSIS_PACKAGE_NAME "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_NSIS_URL_INFO_ABOUT "${CPACK_PACKAGE_HOMEPAGE_URL}")
# NSIS needs a backslash before the file name, as in OrcaSlicer's value.
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_ICON "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/images\\\\JusPrin.ico")
set(CPACK_NSIS_MUI_ICON "${CPACK_PACKAGE_ICON}")
set(CPACK_NSIS_MUI_UNIICON "${CPACK_PACKAGE_ICON}")
# The executable keeps OrcaSlicer's file name; the shortcuts are called JusPrin.
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_EXECUTABLES "orca-slicer;JusPrin")
# Not used (the generator is NSIS), but never OrcaSlicer's upgrade code.
set(CPACK_WIX_UPGRADE_GUID "4f6d1c0e-6a3b-4b0e-9a57-3d2c8e1f7b42")

# Keep OrcaSlicer's architecture suffix (_x64, _arm64) and swap the rest.
set(_jusprin_orca_file_prefix "OrcaSlicer_Windows_Installer_V${SoftFever_VERSION}")
string(FIND "${CPACK_PACKAGE_FILE_NAME}" "${_jusprin_orca_file_prefix}" _jusprin_prefix_at)
if (NOT _jusprin_prefix_at EQUAL 0)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "OrcaSlicer's installer name changed to '${CPACK_PACKAGE_FILE_NAME}'; "
                        "update src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/packaging.cmake to match.")
endif ()
string(REPLACE "${_jusprin_orca_file_prefix}" "JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V${JUSPRIN_VERSION}"
       CPACK_PACKAGE_FILE_NAME "${CPACK_PACKAGE_FILE_NAME}")

# On Windows, OrcaSlicer makes itself the handler of orcaslicer:// links each
# time it starts and when its Preferences dialog closes (GUI_App.cpp), without
# asking. JusPrin leaves those links to OrcaSlicer; the links it opens are the
# ones a person chooses in its Preferences (JusPrin/Preferences).
if (SLIC3R_GUI)
    target_compile_definitions(libslic3r_gui PRIVATE SLIC3R_NO_ORCASLICER_URL_ASSOCIATION)
endif ()
# Included by CMakeLists, edited by the build script
# (the version numbers are generated by the build script from the git current label)

set(SLIC3R_APP_NAME "JusPrin")
set(SLIC3R_APP_KEY "JusPrin")

if(NOT DEFINED BBL_RELEASE_TO_PUBLIC)
set(BBL_RELEASE_TO_PUBLIC "1")

## 🚀 What's New in v1.4.0

- **🐧 Official Linux support (AppImage)**
  - We now provide a portable **AppImage** build for Linux. Download, make it executable, and run—no installation required.

- **Upstream sync: OrcaSlicer v2.3.1**
  - The codebase is now up to date with **OrcaSlicer v2.3.1**, bringing in the latest upstream improvements and fixes.

- **Expanded printer model support**
  - Added compatibility for many of the latest 3D printers across popular brands such as **Phrozen**.

- **Numerous bug fixes**
  - Addressed a wide range of stability, performance, and usability issues reported since v1.3.0.
  - Multiple improvements to print-park (idle/homing) behaviors for smoother operations.

- **Massive codebase improvements**
  - Thousands of lines of code updated.
  - Improved reliability, maintainability, and overall performance.

---

📄 **Changelog**: *For the full list of commits and technical details, see the commit history for [v1.4.0](../../compare/v1.3.0...jusprin/v1.4.0).*

1	=== fa2442a7bd App menus: the same menus on every screen, Print and Printer menus, and Cmd+S saves a version instead of writing over the opened 3MF
2	The app's menus were still OrcaSlicer's. While the JusPrin shell is
3	installed, AppMenus now rearranges them in place and adds JusPrin's
4	commands. Classic view gets OrcaSlicer's menus back exactly.
5	
6	- The same menus show on every screen, Home included. A command that
7	  can't run there is greyed out, never hidden. An OrcaSlicer item is
8	  removed only when it can never run in JusPrin.
9	- File: New project, Open…, Open recent (JusPrin's saved projects),
10	  Save (Cmd/Ctrl+S: saves now and pins a version), Version history…,
11	  Import, and Export, which starts with Project 3MF… on Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+S.
12	  New Window, Save Project, Save Project as and Sync Presets are gone.
13	- View: Home, the Plates and project panel and AI panel toggles,
14	  OrcaSlicer's camera and display items, and Switch to classic view….
15	  Show G-code Window and Reset Window Layout are gone.
16	- Print (new): the header's slice, check, print and export actions.
17	- Printer (new): Add a printer…, Printer settings…, Filament settings…,
18	  their Ask AI rows, and Calibrate…. They work from Home.
19	- Help: adds Ask AI… and Report a problem… (a prefilled GitHub issue).
20	  Setup Wizard and Show Tip of the Day are gone.
21	- On Windows, Quit reads Exit.
22	
23	On the Mac these are the menu bar; on Windows and Linux, the File
24	button and the title-bar drop-down. OrcaSlicer's items stay in the
25	wxMenu that made them, because their handlers are bound there.
26	MainFrame.cpp is unchanged. The one OrcaSlicer-owned line is a
27	GetFileMenu() getter in BBLTopbar.hpp. A merge-tree simulation against
28	upstream/main merges it cleanly and adds no new conflicts.
29	
30	Bug fixed along the way: with a 3MF opened, pressing Cmd+S rewrote that
31	3MF on disk. MainFrame binds its own key hook after the shell installs,
32	and wx runs the most recently bound handler first, so OrcaSlicer's Save
33	always got the key before JusPrin. AppMenus now binds its key hook one
34	event-loop turn after install, once MainFrame's constructor is done.
35	
36	Tested on macOS:
37	- Shell harness: default, --file-opening, --stock and --classic-switch
38	  all pass. New checks cover the menu layout, greyed items on Home, and
39	  exact restoration in classic view. Cmd+S and File › Save must leave
40	  the opened 3MF unchanged and save a version; that check failed before
41	  the key-hook fix.
42	- Live: posted Cmd+D then Cmd+S to the running app. The opened 3MF stayed
43	  byte-for-byte the same, and a new pinned version was saved.
44	
45	Tested on Windows (GCP test VM, MSVC): the menu code compiles, and
46	=== 8cc11b66ac Offer a way back to the JusPrin view from classic view
47	Classic OrcaSlicer view had no way back to JusPrin short of editing the
48	config and restarting. While the shell is off, a banner above the
49	Notebook ("You're in the classic OrcaSlicer view." with Back to JusPrin)
50	and a "Switch to JusPrin view" row at the end of OrcaSlicer's View menu
51	now reinstall the shell over the same frame. The choice is session-only:
52	jusprin_shell is never written. A start with the shell off or a failed
53	install offers the same way back.
54	
55	Going back over the same project keeps its conversation: the shell
56	leaving hands its document to the next one, which adopts it only when
57	OrcaSlicer's project session and auxiliary directory are unchanged. A
58	project replaced or reset in classic view starts its own.
59	
60	Everything is in fork-owned files under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/; no
61	OrcaSlicer-owned file changes. The shell harness's --classic-switch run
62	now makes two round trips (View-menu row, then banner) and --stock
63	returns through the banner; --classic-switch-capture saves the window.
64	
65	Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
66	
67	
68	=== deeb27d07d Set the agent up in one place: Preferences › Agent
69	Every surface that needs the agent and finds none now shows its own
70	not-set-up state with one action that opens Preferences on its Agent
71	section (Kenneth's decisions of 2026-10-23, canvas board "Agent setup ·
72	one door"). When the window closes with an agent, the surface carries on
73	with it live and nothing is sent for the person; closing it without one
74	changes nothing.
75	
76	- Print-issue bubble: with no agent ready it draws one full-width primary
77	  button, "Set up the agent...", in place of Ask AI / Resolve with AI, and
78	  stays open behind the window. Three dots, not an ellipsis: the canvas
79	  font has Latin-1 only. The "Set up now / Not now" MessageDialog
80	  (offer_agent_setup) and open_agent_setup are gone.
81	- Agent pane: its offer, setup bar and chat-list row send shell_action
82	  open_preferences with section agent. The in-pane chooser and key screen
83	  (Setup.tsx), the connected banner, the embedded setup-only page mode
84	  (AgentPageMode::EmbeddedSetup, ?embedded=1), AgentHost::request_setup,
85	  the open_setup message and the setup-completed listener are removed.
86	- Printer panel: its offer opens Preferences › Agent too and the panel
87	  stays open. Its runtime is built at open(), so after the window changes
88	  the agent settings the shell has the open panel reload its agent
89	  (PrinterPanel::reload_agent_config); the greeting then continues.
90	- SetupLocalTool no longer shows the previous tool's error when
91	  Preferences opens it for another tool.
92	
93	Tests: the pane's key-row and AI-tool tests move to the Preferences page;
94	new Vitest cases for each entry point; the shell harness drives the
95	bubble (--print-issues), the pane (--live-agent-unavailable) and the
96	printer panel (--printer-setup) through Preferences, cancel and setup.
97	
98	
99	=== 170d1ae080 Add Anthropic and OpenRouter as Agent providers behind one provider-neutral turn loop
100	The in-app Agent talked to one API, OpenAI's Responses API, through
101	OpenAIResponsesAgent, which mixed the tool-call turn loop with that
102	wire format and with OpenAI-specific choices. Adding a second provider
103	would have meant a second copy of the loop.
104	
105	ProviderAgent now owns the loop and a provider-neutral transcript: the
106	instructions, the tools offered, the earlier conversation, this turn's
107	user content, and one step per response holding the provider's own
108	record of its reply (kept verbatim, because both OpenAI and Anthropic
109	want it echoed back unchanged) with the results of the calls it made.
110	Every rule the old class enforced is unchanged: calls run one at a time
111	in the order written, a failed call answers the rest unrun, unknown or
112	invalid calls are refused back at most twice a turn, images follow
113	results, fired skills are sent once on OpenAI, and late events from a
114	cancelled request are dropped.
115	
116	A codec per API family turns that transcript into a request and each
117	streamed payload into neutral events. ResponsesCodec serves OpenAI and
118	OpenRouter; its request bodies are byte-identical to the old adapter's,
119	checked against the shell harness's recorded bodies. AnthropicCodec
120	serves the Messages API: system and tool cache breakpoints, tool_use and
121	tool_result replay, same-role merging, images inside tool results, call
122	arguments assembled from streamed fragments, every stop reason mapped,
123	and the keywords Anthropic's strict mode rejects (minimum, maximum,
124	minLength, maxLength, maxItems) moved from each tool's schema into the
125	property description, so the registry keeps its full schemas for native
126	validation and for MCP clients. On Anthropic a fired skill stays in place
127	on later requests of the same turn, because dropping it counts as editing
128	history and Opus 5.5 then rejects replayed thinking.
129	
130	Providers are data in ProviderProfile: family, endpoint, auth header,
131	fixed headers, default model, output limit and display name. OpenRouter
132	defaults to the same model as OpenAI; Anthropic to claude-opus-5-5 with
133	a 64000-token output limit. Setup and configuration build the agent
134	through one factory keyed by provider, and JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT
135	overrides whichever endpoint is active (JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT still
136	works). The setup page offers OpenAI, OpenRouter and Anthropic, with
137	OpenAI still the default tab. OpenAIResponsesAgent remains as a thin
138	subclass so the harness compiles unchanged.
139	
140	Tests: the adapter tests are split into loop tests driven through a
141	scripted fake codec and wire tests per codec; a conformance test drives
142	one scripted turn through both codecs and requires identical events;
143	unit tests cover the schema projection. test_provider_live.cpp holds
144	=== 644f8bfaff Add local MCP bridge, discovery, and client setup
145	External AI clients can reach the running JusPrin project through a bundled
146	stdio helper and stable discovery file. Calls share the native registry,
147	coordinator, approval UI, and Orca workspace commands.
148	
149	- Start loopback MCP with the Agent panel, without an enable switch or token.
150	- Publish instance-owned discovery and follow restarts/port changes.
151	- Support legacy stdio clients, modern HTTP, progress, cancellation, bounded
152	  IO, and explicit offline/unknown-outcome errors without mutation retries.
153	- Expose workspace_inspect, inspect_selection, and duplicate_object through
154	  MCP; keep internal history commands and attachment import private.
155	- Render external approvals independently of in-app chat messages.
156	- Add confirmed client setup, guarded JSON edits, Windows install rules,
157	  and early Linux AppImage dispatch through fork-owned helper scripts.
158	- Keep one self-contained tool-extension guide aligned with actual inputs,
159	  outputs, exposure, protocol projections, and unverified release gates.
160	  Process-settings tools remain unimplemented.
161	
162	Verification on macOS before commit:
163	- App/helper/native-harness build and UI production build passed.
164	- 152 Agent tests / 1,699 assertions; 63 UI tests passed.
165	- 17 Python process/launcher tests passed; one Linux-only test skipped.
166	- Native MCP bridge, normal shell, and stock-mode scenarios passed.
167	- Guide links and its seven-entry registry table checked against source.
168	Earlier real Claude Code/Codex CLI tests covered read, reject, approve,
169	restart, and offline behavior using session-only configuration. Persistent
170	one-click setup and GUI-client workflows remain unverified, as do full
171	Windows/Linux GUI releases and macOS universal signing/notarization.
172	
173	Fork stewardship, measured September 4, 2026:

179	Existing conflicts: GUI_ObjectList.cpp must retain relocated rename
180	snapshots with localized labels, not duplicate the old snapshot; Plater.cpp
181	must keep both network includes and ProjectState, and both toolbar-image
182	invalidation and project notifications; Plater.hpp must keep both upstream
183	filament-index helpers and the grouped fork declarations. Choosing only one
184	side would lose behavior. No actual rebase or merge was performed.
185	
186	Both changed upstream-owned files also passed git merge-file using their
187	working contents, the same base, and current upstream. src/CMakeLists.txt
